answer: A film that made a lasting impression on me was a drama I watched a couple of years ago about a family overcoming hardship. The story followed a father who loses his livelihood and struggles to keep his children in school, while trying to hide his worries from them. On the surface it was a simple story, but it dealt with its themes in a genuinely [[profound]] way. I watched it at home on a quiet evening with my parents, expecting light entertainment, and ended up completely [[absorbed]]. What impressed me most was how realistic and emotionally honest it was; the characters felt like real people rather than actors. The acting was wonderfully [[understated]], with no dramatic speeches, just small looks and silences that said everything. There was one scene where the father quietly skips his own meal so the children can eat, and the whole room went silent. By the end, I was genuinely moved, and I found myself thinking about it for days afterwards. My father, who ran a small business for many years, went unusually quiet, and I think it reminded him of some difficult times of his own. It explored ideas about resilience and family in a way that really [[resonated]] with me. Honestly, I think the mark of a great film is that it stays with you long after the credits roll, and this one certainly did. It was far more than mere entertainment; it offered a real [[insight]] into the human condition. I have recommended it to many friends since, and it remains one of my favourite films.

followUps.answer: Yes, but not too soon. It is quite emotionally heavy, so I would save it for the right mood. I suspect I would notice even more details the second time around.

followUps.q: Do you prefer watching films at home or in the cinema?
followUps.answer: Mostly at home, partly because Sirajganj has limited cinema options. Watching with my family also means we can pause and talk about it, which I actually enjoy more than a silent cinema hall.
